title: Beth definability: when uniqueness forces a formula
summary: Prove that a relation uniquely determined by a first-order theory has one uniform definition in the old language.
abstract: A theory can determine a new relation without presenting a formula for it. For example, a nonempty set of two-sided identity elements is fixed once the binary operation is fixed, even if the axioms only describe what its members do. Beth’s theorem says that this kind of uniqueness always yields a definition in first-order logic. We compare two proposed interpretations of the new relation, use finitely many axioms to express their agreement, and apply interpolation to remove both new names. The resulting formula works in every model of the theory. We also distinguish uniqueness from existence: some old structures may have no expansion satisfying the theory at all.
